title: SLO synthesis: latency vs cost waterfall (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note is a working draft that synthesizes microbenchmarks into actionable SLO tradeoffs for product-facing inference routes. Goal: give product/infra a single-page view showing how much extra cost buys X ms tail latency improvement across realistic workload slices.

Test harness and assumptions:
- Hardware: H100-80GB (pinned) and A100-80GB (baseline).
- Models: redwood-7b-v2 (float16), redwood-7b-v2-int4, redwood-13b-v1 (float16).
- Workloads: chat-session (avg-turn 80 tokens, 6 turns/session), stateless-single (avg 120 tokens), high-concurrency burst (poisson lambda bursts).
- KV cache hit scenarios: 0%, 50%, 90%.
- Batching: min-batch 1 (real-time) vs opportunistic window 20ms.
- Cost model: infra cost normalized to $/GPU-hour (H100=$6.40/hr, A100=$4.10/hr) + amortized memory footprint & infra overhead. Token cost computed by amortizing per-request GPU time into $ per 1k tokens.

Key metrics captured (per model/hardware/kv-hit): p50, p95, p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (throughput), cost_per_1k_tokens ($).

Summary findings (short):
- Small quant (int4) on redwood-7b-v2 reduces cost per 1k tokens by ~38% with median latency impact <6% on H100 for stateless.
- For sessionized chat with 90% KV hit, effective p95 improves by ~40% vs 0% hit because KV avoids autoregressive decoding for prefix tokens; cost per session drops roughly 25%.
- Opportunistic batching (20ms window) reduces cost per token by 18-28% but increases p95 by 12-22ms depending on model; useful for non-interactive routes.

Representative text tables (H100):

Model | KV-hit | Workload | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tks/sec | $/1k-tks
------|--------|----------|---------|---------|---------|--------|--------
redwood-7b-v2-fp16 | 0% | stateless-120 | 42 | 118 | 235 | 480 | 0.80
redwood-7b-v2-int4 | 0% | stateless-120 | 46 | 128 | 260 | 680 | 0.50
redwood-7b-v2-fp16 | 90% | chat-80/6 | 28 | 72 | 145 | 640 | 0.62
redwood-13b-v1-fp16 | 0% | stateless-120 | 85 | 240 | 430 | 210 | 1.95

Waterfall view: incremental $ to reduce p95 by X ms (chat workload, H100, redwood-7b-v2):
- Baseline (0% KV, no batching, fp16): p95=118ms, $/1k-tks=0.80
- Add opportunistic batching (20ms): p95=135ms (+17ms), $/1k-tks=0.66 (-17%)
- Switch to int4 quant: p95=145ms (+27ms vs baseline), $/1k-tks=0.46 (-42%)
- Add KV cache @90%: p95=72ms (-46ms vs baseline), $/1k-tks=0.62 (-22%)
- Combined (int4 + KV 90% + batching): p95=68ms (-50ms), $/1k-tks=0.32 (-60%)

Interpretation notes:
- Cost-first optimizations (quant, batching) reduce $/token significantly, but can raise tail latency unless KV cache is effective.
- For interactive user-facing chat routes, KV cache provides the most consistent p95 improvement per dollar spent because it reduces decoding work on the happy path.
- For high-throughput backplane routes (embeddings, rerank), batching wins.

Simple SLO knobs proposal (for product):
- SLO tier A (interactive): p95 <= 120ms, target cost <= 0.75 $/1k-tks => recommended: fp16, KV bias, reserved H100 pool, prewarm slots.
- SLO tier B (bulk-inference): p95 <= 250ms, target cost <= 0.60 $/1k-tks => recommended: int4, opportunistic batching 20ms, A100 acceptable.
- SLO tier C (best-effort cheap): p95 <= 500ms, cost <= 0.35 $/1k-tks => recommended: int4 + aggressive caching, burst to spot capacity.

ASCII mini-plot: p95 vs $/1k tokens (points sorted by p95)
|p95(ms)	| $/1k-tks | label
|----------------------------------------|
| 68 	| 0.32 	| int4+KV+batch
| 72 	| 0.62 	| KV only
| 118 	| 0.80 	| baseline fp16
| 240 	| 1.95 	| rwd-13b fp16

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Validate A100 cost baseline with finance (numbers are rounded).
- Expand harness to 2K concurrent sessions to check preemption and multi-tenant noise.
- Run same sweep on private-deploy build (VPC) -- networking differences may add 6-18ms tail.
- Produce per-route recommended defaults and add to console rollout templates.

References and quick links: confluence:OBS/SLO-synthesis, JIRA:OBS-887, github:benchmarks/pull/321

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Miguel: add your per-shard mem profiles (we used coarse mem numbers).
- Aisha: can you sanity-check p99 outliers from yesterday's traces? I'm seeing odd plateaus at ~350ms on low QPS runs.

End of draft.
